title: Powers of a regular sequence
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M$ an $R$-module, $f_1,\dots,f_r\in R$ and $e_1,\dots,e_r>0$ integers. Then $f_1,\dots,f_r$ is an $M$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] if and only if $f_1^{e_1},\dots,f_r^{e_r}$ is an $M$-regular sequence.

proof.text: Reformulation of the definition [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. For an $R$-module $N$ and $g_1,\dots,g_s\in R$ ($s\ge0$) say that $g_1,\dots,g_s$ is *weakly $N$-regular* if condition (1) of the definition holds: $g_i$ is a nonzerodivisor on $N/(g_1,\dots,g_{i-1})N$ for $i=1,\dots,s$ (the empty sequence is weakly $N$-regular). Then $f_1,\dots,f_r$ is $M$-regular iff it is weakly $M$-regular and $M/(f_1,\dots,f_r)M\neq0$. Moreover, for $s\ge1$, $g_1,\dots,g_s$ is weakly $N$-regular iff $g_1$ is a nonzerodivisor on $N$ and $g_2,\dots,g_s$ is weakly $N/g_1N$-regular: for $2\le i\le s$ the $R$-modules $(N/g_1N)/(g_2,\dots,g_{i-1})(N/g_1N)$ and $N/(g_1,\dots,g_{i-1})N$ are equal (both are $N$ modulo $g_1N+g_2N+\dots+g_{i-1}N$), so multiplication by $g_i$ is the same map on both.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07DV (lemma-regular-sequence-powers), proof (the reduction 'by induction applied to M/f_1M'); definition Tag 00LF

proof.text: One element. Let $N$ be an $R$-module, $f\in R$, $e\ge1$. (a) $f$ is a nonzerodivisor on $N$ iff $f^e$ is: if $f$ is one and $f^ex=0$, then $f\cdot f^{e-1}x=0$ gives $f^{e-1}x=0$, and by induction on $e$ $x=0$; if $f^e$ is one and $fx=0$, then $f^ex=f^{e-1}(fx)=0$, so $x=0$ (Stacks' facts (a) and (b)). (b) If $f$ is a nonzerodivisor on $N$ and $e\ge2$, then $0\to N/fN\xrightarrow{f^{e-1}}N/f^eN\to N/f^{e-1}N\to0$ is a short exact sequence of $R$-modules, where the first map sends $x\bmod fN$ to $f^{e-1}x\bmod f^eN$ (well defined as $f^{e-1}\cdot fN=f^eN$) and the second is the projection ($f^eN\subseteq f^{e-1}N$). Indeed the projection is surjective with kernel $f^{e-1}N/f^eN$, which is the image of the first map; and if $f^{e-1}x=f^ey$ then $f^{e-1}(x-fy)=0$, so $x=fy\in fN$ by (a), i.e. the first map is injective.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07DV (lemma-regular-sequence-powers), proof (case r = 1, facts (a), (b); the short exact sequence with the map f_1^{e-1})

proof.text: The nonvanishing condition (2). Let $J=(f_1,\dots,f_r)$ and $J'=(f_1^{e_1},\dots,f_r^{e_r})$. Since $J'\subseteq J$, $M=J'M$ implies $M=JM$. Conversely, if $M=JM$ then $M=J(JM)=J^2M=\dots=J^nM$ for all $n\ge1$; for $n=e_1+\dots+e_r-r+1$ the ideal $J^n$ is generated by the monomials $f_1^{a_1}\cdots f_r^{a_r}$ with $a_1+\dots+a_r=n$, each of which has some $a_i\ge e_i$ (otherwise $\sum a_i\le\sum(e_i-1)<n$) and so lies in $J'$; hence $M=J^nM\subseteq J'M$. Thus $M/JM\neq0$ iff $M/J'M\neq0$.

proof.text: Raising the first element, forward direction. Let $N$ be an $R$-module, $f\in R$ a nonzerodivisor on $N$, $g_1,\dots,g_s\in R$ and $e\ge1$. If $g_1,\dots,g_s$ is weakly $N/fN$-regular (Step 1), then it is weakly $N/f^eN$-regular. Induction on $e$: for $e=1$ there is nothing to prove. For $e\ge2$ take the short exact sequence $0\to N/fN\to N/f^eN\to N/f^{e-1}N\to0$ of Step 2(b); $g_1,\dots,g_s$ is weakly regular on $N/fN$ by hypothesis and on $N/f^{e-1}N$ by the induction hypothesis, so by part (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-short-exact-sequence] it is weakly regular on $N/f^eN$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07DV (lemma-regular-sequence-powers), proof ('Suppose that f_1, ..., f_r is an M-regular sequence ... By Lemma 0F1T f_2, ..., f_r is M/f_1^eM-regular')

proof.text: Raising the first element, converse direction. Let $N$, $f$ (a nonzerodivisor on $N$) and $g_1,\dots,g_s$ be as in Step 4, $e\ge2$, and suppose $g_1,\dots,g_s$ is weakly $N/f^eN$-regular. Put $A=N/fN$, $B=N/f^eN$, $C=N/f^{e-1}N$, $K_i=(g_1,\dots,g_i)$. We show by induction on $0\le i\le s$: ($P_i$) $g_1,\dots,g_i$ is weakly $A$-regular and the sequence $0\to A/K_iA\to B/K_iB\to C/K_iC\to0$ induced by the sequence of Step 2(b) is exact. $P_0$ is Step 2(b). Assume $P_i$ with $i<s$. By hypothesis $g_{i+1}$ is a nonzerodivisor on $B/K_iB$; by $P_i$, $A/K_iA\to B/K_iB$ is an injective $R$-linear map, which commutes with multiplication by $g_{i+1}$, so $g_{i+1}$ is a nonzerodivisor on $A/K_iA$, and $g_1,\dots,g_{i+1}$ is weakly $A$-regular. By Step 4 applied with the exponent $e-1\ge1$ to the sequence $g_1,\dots,g_{i+1}$, it is weakly $C$-regular; in particular $g_{i+1}$ is a nonzerodivisor on $C/K_iC$. Apply the snake lemma [lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-modules] to the two copies of the exact row $0\to A/K_iA\to B/K_iB\to C/K_iC\to0$ with vertical maps multiplication by $g_{i+1}$: the kernel of $g_{i+1}$ on $C/K_iC$ is $0$, so $\operatorname{coker}\to\operatorname{coker}$ on the first two terms is injective, and the map of the last two cokernels is surjective since $B/K_iB\to C/K_iC$ is; as $(X/K_iX)/g_{i+1}(X/K_iX)=X/K_{i+1}X$ for $X=A,B,C$, this is the exactness of $0\to A/K_{i+1}A\to B/K_{i+1}B\to C/K_{i+1}C\to0$, which proves $P_{i+1}$. $P_s$ says that $g_1,\dots,g_s$ is weakly $N/fN$-regular. Together with Step 4 (and the trivial case $e=1$): for $f$ a nonzerodivisor on $N$ and $e\ge1$, $g_1,\dots,g_s$ is weakly $N/fN$-regular iff it is weakly $N/f^eN$-regular.

proof.text: Conclusion. By induction on $r$ we show, for every $R$-module $N$: $f_1,\dots,f_r$ is weakly $N$-regular iff $f_1^{e_1},\dots,f_r^{e_r}$ is. For $r=0$ both hold. For $r\ge1$, by Step 1, $f_1,\dots,f_r$ is weakly $N$-regular iff $f_1$ is a nonzerodivisor on $N$ and $f_2,\dots,f_r$ is weakly $N/f_1N$-regular; by the induction hypothesis for the module $N/f_1N$ the latter is equivalent to $f_2^{e_2},\dots,f_r^{e_r}$ being weakly $N/f_1N$-regular; when $f_1$ is a nonzerodivisor on $N$ this is equivalent by Step 5 (with $f=f_1$, $e=e_1$) to $f_2^{e_2},\dots,f_r^{e_r}$ being weakly $N/f_1^{e_1}N$-regular; and $f_1$ is a nonzerodivisor on $N$ iff $f_1^{e_1}$ is (Step 2(a)). By Step 1 again the result is equivalent to $f_1^{e_1},\dots,f_r^{e_r}$ being weakly $N$-regular. Taking $N=M$ and combining with Step 3 and the first part of Step 1 ($M$-regular = weakly $M$-regular plus nonvanishing of the quotient) gives the lemma for [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].
